title: The Pantheon’s 1,900-year-old dome still holds a concrete record
body: Rebuilt under Emperor Hadrian and probably dedicated around AD 126, the Pantheon in Rome still has the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world. Its interior is 43.3 meters wide and exactly as tall, so a perfect sphere would fit inside. Roman builders made the concrete lighter toward the top, moving from heavy travertine to porous tufa and pumice, and left an open oculus at the crown.

slides.question: How did Roman builders keep the top of the dome light?
options: Porous tufa and pumice in the mix
slides.explanation: The concrete gets lighter toward the top, moving from heavy travertine to porous tufa and pumice, and an open oculus sits at the crown.
